# Demo scenario evidence checkpoints

These are independent expectations for [demo-evidence.jsonl](demo-evidence.jsonl), not a record of an executed test. They apply to the common native receiver. Values are fictional.

## Observation conditions

The scenario starts its 20-second pass at the first successful Open. Registration takes time, so early samples can be missed. The input holds pitch at `-π/12` radians and bank at `π/6` radians. With active flight and fresh eligible attitude, the expected output is pitch `15` degrees and roll `-30` degrees. Compare these values within `1e-9` degrees; the decimal inputs approximate those angles to better than that tolerance. Check native radians within `1e-12` radians. These numeric tolerances address decimal and floating-point conversion, not scheduler delay.

The following offsets are scenario-clock positions, not journal timestamps. Use a controlled clock at the DLL seam for exact positions. For a real application run, retain a run-start reference and delimit windows using observable events and a measured uncertainty bound. If the start, queue delay, or SSE delivery cannot bound a window away from its neighboring segments, mark that checkpoint inconclusive. Journal `elapsed_us` measures time from journal start at recording, not Demo emission time; receipt can lag emission. Do not infer an exact scenario position from it. A 50 ms frame period is nominal, not a bound on scheduling or queue delay. Record the actual window and bound separately from numeric tolerance.

| Pass and scenario offset | Authored input and independent expectation | Receipt and final observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First, 0–5 s | IAS holds at 100 kt. After registration, flags 0 request repeated equal observations. | `instrument_sample` for IAS reports 100 repeatedly. While active with fresh attitude, SSE `ias_kt` is 100. Check a window longer than 1000 ms with continued receipts and live SSE to distinguish fresh equal values from one cached sample. |
| First, 5–10 s | IAS ramps from 100 to 150 kt. At exactly 7.5 s, `100 + (150 - 100) × 2.5 / 5 = 125` kt; at 7.45 and 7.55 s the values are 124.5 and 125.5 kt. | At a controlled position, compare the native value within `1e-9` kt. Compare SSE only when the captured snapshot is known to contain that receipt; it may contain a later value. For a real run, use an independently bounded position interval and calculate its endpoints at 10 kt/s; do not require an exact 125 observation. SSE may skip it. |
| First, 10–14 s | IAS gap produces no IAS packets. ALT continues at 1000 ft. | After the last IAS receipt ages at least 1000 ms, an active live SSE snapshot omits `ias_kt` and retains `altitude_ft: 1000`, provided ALT and attitude remain fresh. Do not infer immediate expiry at 10 s or count packets against SSE events. |
| First, 15–17 s | Normal pause at 15 s; resume at 17 s. IAS holds at 150 kt. | Observe pause event flag 8 and a `paused` snapshot with null attitude and omitted optional fields. After flag 0, require a new eligible attitude before `live`; then fresh IAS may appear as 150. Paused receipts alone cannot authorize resume. |
| First end and second start, 19–22 s | Active pause at 19 s; the cursor loops at 20 s. The `off` event at pass offset 2 s occurs at absolute offset 22 s. | Observe flag 4 and `paused` across the boundary. No implicit resume occurs at 20 s. After the explicit flag 0 and fresh eligible samples, live IAS is 100 kt. The later pass uses later deadlines; it does not reset the clock or lifecycle state. |

A sparse IAS-only or event-only scenario has no eligible attitude. Its receipt evidence must not be asserted as a live IAS snapshot. A gap in either primary attitude component suppresses the grouped packet, so the other component cannot refresh attitude alone. With no fresh eligible attitude, SSE omits optional values and carries null attitude; the state depends on lifecycle and freshness.

Other independent normalization examples are heading 370 degrees → `heading_deg: 10`, ball -63.5 → `slip_skid: -0.5`, and 29.92 inHg → `baro_setting.pressure_hpa: 1013.207489067664`. These require fresh inputs and an eligible attitude. Compare within `1e-9` in the respective output units. Selected heading 370 degrees also yields 10 only while the availability gate is 1; selected altitude 2500 ft is omitted when radio mode is 1. These are calculation checkpoints, not claims that the focused scenario supplies those fields.

For the IAS estimator, a controlled sequence of `(100, 0 ms)`, `(102.5, 250 ms)`, and `(105, 500 ms)` yields `(105 - 100) / 0.5 = 10 kt/s`. Equal samples over the same interval yield zero. This is a receiver-time calculation, not a literal scenario field. A real run may have different receipt intervals and skipped frames; calculate against independently observed acquisition times only when available. Otherwise do not claim an exact trend. A 500 ms IAS silence clears the trend; IAS itself expires at 1000 ms. No other field refreshes either IAS timer.

## Evidence record

Record the scenario file and SHA-256, application and DLL paths and hashes, source revision, build and launch commands, and journal session ID. Record the run-start reference, pass and window, observed events, uncertainty bounds, capture method, actual values, and results. Keep the scenario clock, journal elapsed clock, and SSE capture clock distinct. A missing bounded relationship is an evidence gap, not a new timestamp in the native ABI. The [test evidence procedure](../../docs/testing/evidence.md#test-evidence-records) covers provenance and result status.
